t: 2167. Minimum Time to Remove All Cars Containing Illegal Goods
o: Any optimal plan removes some prefix [0, i) from the left (cost i), some suffix (j, n) from the right (cost n-1-j), and every remaining '1' in the middle segment [i, j] individually at cost 2 ('0's in the middle can stay). So the answer is min over 0 <= i <= j < n of i + (n-1-j) + 2*ones(i..j), also considering removing everything from the ends (cost n). Rewriting with prefix one-counts P: cost = (n-1-j) + 2*P[j+1] + min over i <= j of (i - 2*P[i]), and that inner minimum can be maintained incrementally as j grows, giving O(n). Example 1 verifies: choosing i=2, j=5 gives 2 + 1 + 2*1 = 5.
k: Every plan decomposes into a left-removed prefix, a right-removed suffix, and middle '1's removed at cost 2 each.
With prefix sums of ones, the objective separates into a j-term plus a running minimum over i of (i - 2*P[i]).

a.i: Enumerate the right boundary j while maintaining the best (i - 2*P[i]) among valid left boundaries; each step is O(1).
s: Build P where P[i] = number of ones in s[0..i-1].
Initialize run = i - 2*P[i] for i = 0 (value 0) and best = n (strip everything from the ends).
For each j from 0 to n-1: fold i = j into run, then best = min(best, (n-1-j) + 2*P[j+1] + run).
a.t: O(n) — one prefix-sum pass plus one enumeration pass
a.sp: O(n) for the prefix array (reducible to O(1) by folding the count into the loop)

w: Sanity anchors: all-'0' input costs n (just peel the ends), all-'1' input costs n as well (peeling beats paying 2 per car). Pitfalls: forgetting the pure end-removal baseline of n, and mixing up whether middle '0's cost anything (they do not). Follow-up: what if middle removal cost were 3 — the same decomposition works with the coefficient changed.
